   172	+`baton loop` is the goal supervisor. It runs a repo-local `loop.json` plan through headless writer and reviewer roles from `baton.config.json`, records state in gitignored `.handoff/loop/`, and keeps the handoff bundle ready if a child session dies on usage limits. It supervises the boring parts that otherwise get lost between harnesses: phase position, review iteration counts, child logs, smoke-test approval, and park/resume/escalate decisions.
   173	+
   174	+Quickstart:
   175	+
   176	+```sh
   177	+baton loop init "<goal>"
   178	+# edit loop.json: add constraints, set smoke.cmd / smoke.expect, adjust phases if needed
   179	+baton loop run
   180	+```
   181	+
   182	+`baton loop init` writes `loop.json` at the repo root and leaves an existing file untouched. `baton loop run` validates that spec against your role matrix, starts the supervisor, and runs each phase until the goal is approved, parked, or escalated. Runtime files stay under `.handoff/loop/`; the committed contract is `loop.json` plus `baton.config.json`.
   183	+
   184	+If `loop.json` defines a smoke command, the loop stops after the smoke-build slice and writes `.handoff/loop/SMOKE-REVIEW.md` plus `.handoff/loop/smoke-approval.json`. Review the smoke output, copy the token from the approval file or the review note, then continue with:
   185	+
   186	+```sh
   187	+baton loop run --approve-smoke <token>
   188	+```
   189	+
   190	+The token is bound to loop state, smoke command, smoke output, git state, and the child assignment. If anything moved after the review, approval is refused and the run parks for a fresh smoke pass; baton does not spend the full-run budget on stale approval.
   191	+
   192	+Park/resume/escalate behavior is explicit:
   193	+
   194	+| Exit | Meaning | Operator action |
   195	+|---:|---|---|
   196	+| 0 | Done, or paused cleanly awaiting smoke approval | Continue only if a smoke token is requested |
   197	+| 1 | Another live supervisor owns the run lock | Let the live supervisor finish, or recover only after it is provably dead |
   198	+| 2 | Usage/config error | Fix `loop.json`, `baton.config.json`, flags, or root selection |
   199	+| 3 | Escalated | Read `.handoff/loop/ESCALATION.md`; this file is operator-only, not a prompt for the next child |
   200	+| 4 | Parked | Inspect the park reason, then run `baton loop resume` when ready |
   201	+
   202	+A parked run preserves state, logs, and any worktree context for inspection. `baton loop resume` only resumes a parked run; an escalated run needs an operator decision because a review gate hit its cap and baton will not start a hidden sixth attempt.
   203	+

   218	 baton **complements** native configs — AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and `.cursor/rules` stay canonical. It never wraps or proxies a harness. Delete `.handoff/` and everything works as before.
   219	 
   220	+## baton loop
   221	+
   222	+`baton loop` is the goal supervisor. It runs a repo-local `loop.json` plan through headless writer and reviewer roles from `baton.config.json`, records state in gitignored `.handoff/loop/`, and keeps the handoff bundle ready if a child session dies on usage limits. It supervises the boring parts that otherwise get lost between harnesses: phase position, review iteration counts, child logs, smoke-test approval, and park/resume/escalate decisions.
   223	+
   224	+Quickstart:
   225	+
   226	+```sh
   227	+baton loop init "<goal>"
   228	+# edit loop.json: add constraints, set smoke.cmd / smoke.expect, adjust phases if needed
   229	+baton loop run
   230	+```
   231	+
   232	+`baton loop init` writes `loop.json` at the repo root and leaves an existing file untouched. `baton loop run` validates that spec against your role matrix, starts the supervisor, and runs each phase until the goal is approved, parked, or escalated. Runtime files stay under `.handoff/loop/`; the committed contract is `loop.json` plus `baton.config.json`.
   233	+
   234	+If `loop.json` defines a smoke command, the loop stops after the smoke-build slice and writes `.handoff/loop/SMOKE-REVIEW.md` plus `.handoff/loop/smoke-approval.json`. Review the smoke output, copy the token from the approval file or the review note, then continue with:
   235	+
   236	+```sh
   237	+baton loop run --approve-smoke <token>
   238	+```
   239	+
   240	+The token is bound to loop state, smoke command, smoke output, git state, and the child assignment. If anything moved after the review, approval is refused and the run parks for a fresh smoke pass; baton does not spend the full-run budget on stale approval.
   241	+
   242	+Park/resume/escalate behavior is explicit:
   243	+
   244	+| Exit | Meaning | Operator action |
   245	+|---:|---|---|
   246	+| 0 | Done, or paused cleanly awaiting smoke approval | Continue only if a smoke token is requested |
   247	+| 1 | Another live supervisor owns the run lock | Let the live supervisor finish, or recover only after it is provably dead |
   248	+| 2 | Usage/config error | Fix `loop.json`, `baton.config.json`, flags, or root selection |
   249	+| 3 | Escalated | Read `.handoff/loop/ESCALATION.md`; this file is operator-only, not a prompt for the next child |
   250	+| 4 | Parked | Inspect the park reason, then run `baton loop resume` when ready |
   251	+
   252	+A parked run preserves state, logs, and any worktree context for inspection. `baton loop resume` only resumes a parked run; an escalated run needs an operator decision because a review gate hit its cap and baton will not start a hidden sixth attempt.
   253	+
